trace.final_message:
I added `hourglass/gaps.py` and committed it. The full test suite passes, with thirty-three tests in total, and the lint script is clean.

- **`find_gaps(worked, opening)`:** This returns the uncovered stretches as spans, in time order. Overlapping, touching and unordered worked spans are handled by the existing `merge_spans`. If nobody works, the whole opening span is one gap.
- **`gap_labels(worked, opening)`:** This returns one label per gap, for example `gap 12:00-13:00 (60 min)`.
- **Spans outside opening hours:** Any worked span that starts before opening or ends after closing raises `ValueError`. That matches how `Span` already reports bad values. The message names both the span and the opening hours.
- **Tests:** `tests/test_gaps.py` has seven tests. They cover a lunch gap, an empty day, full coverage, overlapping and unordered input, gaps at both ends and in the middle, and a span before opening and one after closing.

I also exported both functions from `hourglass/__init__.py`. I added them to `docs/api.txt` and added a line to `CHANGES.txt`. You did not ask for those, but they match how the earlier commits kept the docs in step.

I followed the Python rules in `CLAUDE.md`. Each new file starts with the owner comment line. Imports are in reverse alphabetical order. Lines are at most sixty characters. Names have at least four letters. There is a `# ---` line above each public function, and I created the files with the Write tool. I also reviewed the staged diff before committing.

One side effect of the "no two blank lines in a row" rule: the new files use a single blank line between top-level definitions. Standard Python style asks for two, so a formatter such as black would change that.

The commit is `69fa012` on `master`.

## Unreleased
- Clearer wording when a span ends before it starts.

## 0.7.1 (2026-07-08)
- normalize_day accepts full day names in any case.

## 0.7.0 (2026-04-22)
- Add format_day_line and day_coverage.
- worker_minutes no longer merges overlaps for the same worker.

## 0.6.0 (2025-12-15)
- Read schedules from CSV.

- Add intersect_spans. Touching spans no longer count as overlapping.
before.docs/api.txt:
hourglass.parsing.parse_clock(text): read a clock time as minutes since midnight
hourglass.parsing.format_clock(minutes): minutes since midnight as HH:MM
hourglass.parsing.parse_span(text): read a range such as 09:00-17:30
hourglass.parsing.format_span(span): a span as start-end text
hourglass.parsing.normalize_day(text): short lowercase day name
hourglass.merging.spans_overlap(first, second): whether two spans share any time
hourglass.merging.intersect_spans(first, second): the part two spans share
hourglass.merging.merge_spans(spans): collapse overlaps into a sorted list
hourglass.merging.total_minutes(spans): minutes covered, overlaps counted once
hourglass.schedule.parse_schedule_text(text): parse schedule CSV held in memory
hourglass.schedule.load_schedule(path): read a schedule CSV from disk
hourglass.schedule.shifts_for_worker(shifts, worker): all shifts for one worker
hourglass.schedule.worker_minutes(shifts): scheduled minutes per worker
hourglass.schedule.day_coverage(shifts, day): merged spans for a day
hourglass.schedule.format_day_line(shifts, day): one text line for a day
